subject: Pilot top-up options: escrow vs invoice-offset for Stratford Analytics
messages:
From: Ethan Miles <ethan.miles@stratford.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot top-up options & invoice handling

Hi Rachel,

Quick one — we burned through our pilot allocation faster than expected after the NER and summarization runs last week. We still have evaluation work to complete (tuning prompts + 1 more integration sprint) and would like to top up capacity for 2–3 weeks. Procurement has pushed back on sending money to an escrow account for something under $25k; they prefer standard PO + invoice flow.

Can you share what flexibility you have on short-term top-ups vs a short extension, and whether Redwood can apply any unused portion as an offset on our next invoice (invoice-offset) instead of holding funds in escrow? If you have suggested contract language procurement would accept, that would speed things up — procurement is on cc (procurement@stratford.ai).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15m if easier.

Ethan

Hi Ethan — thanks for the note and for including procurement.

We can definitely do a short top-up or a short extension; below are two practical options that other customers have used when procurement won’t accept escrow:

Option A — Short top-up (fastest):
- 2-week token bundle: 200k tokens (sufficient for integration sprint + final eval)
- Price: $6,000 (prepaid)
- Redwood issues an invoice on receipt of PO; unused token balance will be issued as a credit note and applied to your next invoice within 45 days.

Option B — 3-week extension with conditional crediting:
- Extend pilot term by 3 weeks; we increase the throughput cap for the extension window.
- Billing: Redwood invoices for the extension up front (or via PO). Unused portion is converted to a credit that appears on the next invoice; if Stratford prefers, we can add a brief amendment clause stating that unused funds will be credited within 60 days.

Practical notes:
- Finance prefers invoice-offset (credit note applied to next invoice) over holding funds in a third-party escrow for amounts under ~$50k — this keeps procurement happy and avoids additional paperwork.
- Legal can sign a 1-paragraph amendment that defines how unused funds are credited; we can share sample language.
- If procurement requires a PO number on the invoice, we’ll include it and map the credit to that PO.

I attached a quick pricing workbook with the token bundles and a sample amendment. If invoice-offset is acceptable to procurement, Option A will be the quickest to execute. If you want the extension route, Option B gives you guaranteed access for the additional weeks.

If it helps I can loop in Kimberly (legal/finance) to confirm the amendment language — Karthik will also drop a calendar invite for a 15m alignment with procurement.

Best,
Rachel

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the breakdown. Procurement's ask: they will require language that ensures any unused prepayment is applied to Stratford's account balance and references the PO number; they don't want third-party escrow for sub-$25k.

Can you provide the concise amendment they can attach to the PO that states: 1) Redwood will apply unused top-up funds to Stratford's account as a credit; 2) the credit will be reflected on the next Redwood invoice and will reference the associated PO number; 3) credit expires in 90 days.

Procurement is happy to sign as long as that language is present. Once we have wording they like, they will issue the PO immediately.

Ethan

Ethan — looping in Kimberly from Legal/Finance. Below is suggested amendment language that aligns with Finance's invoice-offset preference and should be procurement-friendly. I kept it short so it can be appended to your PO: 

---Suggested amendment (one paragraph)---
Redwood Inference will apply any unused funds associated with the agreed pilot top-up (the "Top-Up Amount") to Stratford Analytics' account as a credit. The credit will be reflected on Stratford Analytics' next invoice from Redwood and will reference the PO number provided by Stratford. Any unused credit will expire 90 days from the date the credit is issued.

Kimberly: please confirm the 90-day expiry is acceptable from a finance perspective; if Finance prefers 60 days we can update.

If that wording works for you, Ethan, we'll:
1) Prepare a short amendment document (I attached a draft).
2) Karthik will post an invoice referencing the PO once we receive it.
3) On payment, we mark the invoice as prepaid and Redwood will apply any unused portion as a credit per the amendment.

Next steps: Ethan — if procurement signs off on the paragraph above, send the PO and we’ll generate the invoice this afternoon. Karthik, please go ahead and draft the invoice flow and calendar a quick 15m with procurement if they want to review the mechanics.

Thanks everyone — happy to finalize this today.

Rachel
